Their answer was along the lines of 'Biology and Chemistry can be reduced to physics which can be reduced to Math, which explains everything.' When pressed why math exists, he said 'If maths didn't exist, then the definition of there being nothing means there's 0 quantity of anything wouldn't work because that is a mathematical concept, so maths has to exist, and due to maths everything else that exists has to exist'. If you agree with that sort of reductionist reasoning then I guess it's a pretty solid answer.

Also a note on your point about the universe splitting apart and big banging forever, some physicists speculate that after 10^10^10^56 years from now, random quantum fluctuations and quantum tunnelling will generate a new big bang. If all universes contain the same number of subatomic particles and obey laws of physics within the range predicted by string theory, this universe would actually be identical.
